gate.console:
[kernelloom] Veylith 128-Native v1 booting user program
gate: ok
[kernelloom] user exit 0
gate.source:
; Sigil call gate: a protected counter service reached by a 2-Glyph call, with no kernel involvement per call.
; The service owns a 256-byte region: its code is at the region base (the ONLY entry point a gate allows) and its counter
; lives inside the region. The client seals the region capability into a gate, enters capability mode, and can then reach the
; service only through ccall: it cannot read or write the counter, and cannot jump anywhere else in the service.
.equ USER_BASE, 0x10000
.org USER_BASE
_start:
    li   sp, 0x1F000
    la   v2, svc
    li   v3, 8                   ; 2^8 = 256 bytes, naturally aligned (see .align below)
    li   v4, 7 | 8               ; READ | WRITE | NARROW | GATE
    li   v1, 10
    sys  0                       ; capget
    cseal v30, v1                ; the gate: an opaque token; its base is the one entry point
    li   v1, 11
    sys  0                       ; capability mode: raw loads and stores now trap
    ccall v20, v30               ; v1 = 1
    mv   v10, v1
    ccall v20, v30               ; v1 = 2
    mv   v11, v1
    ccall v20, v30               ; v1 = 3
    mv   v12, v1
    li   v6, 1
    bne  v10, v6, bad
    li   v6, 2
    bne  v11, v6, bad
    li   v6, 3
    bne  v12, v6, bad
    la   v2, msg_ok
    li   v3, 9
    li   v1, 1
    sys  0
    li   v2, 0
    li   v1, 2
    sys  0
bad:
    la   v2, msg_bad
    li   v3, 4
    li   v1, 1
    sys  0
    li   v2, 1
    li   v1, 2
    sys  0
msg_ok:  .ascii "gate: ok\n"
msg_bad: .ascii "BAD\n"
.align 256
svc:                             ; entry: v20 = the service's own data authority, delivered by ccall
    clq  v6, [v20 + 128]
    addi v6, v6, 1
    csq  [v20 + 128], v6
    mv   v1, v6
    cretn
.space 160

gateswitch.console:
[kernelloom] Veylith 128-Native v1 booting user program
gate switching: ok
[kernelloom] user exit 0
gateswitch.source:
; Gate calls survive context switches: the gate's return link is saved per task. Both tasks enter the same service, and the
; service yields to the other task in the MIDDLE of the call. Each task must still return to its own caller.
.equ USER_BASE, 0x10000
.org USER_BASE
_start:
    li   sp, 0x1F000
    la   v2, svc
    li   v3, 8
    li   v4, 7 | 8
    li   v1, 10
    sys  0                       ; capget
    cseal v30, v1
    li   v1, 11
    sys  0                       ; capability mode, inherited by the worker
    la   v2, worker
    li   v3, 0x1E000
    mv   v4, v30                 ; the gate token is the worker's argument
    li   v1, 6
    sys  0
    mv   v24, v1
    ccall v20, v30               ; yields inside the service, comes back here
    mv   v10, v1
    li   v1, 9                   ; recv the worker's result
    sys  0
    mv   v11, v1
    add  v12, v10, v11
    li   v6, 3
    bne  v12, v6, bad            ; the two results are 1 and 2 in some order
    beq  v10, v11, bad
    mv   v2, v24
    li   v1, 7
    sys  0                       ; join
    la   v2, msg_ok
    li   v3, 19
    li   v1, 1
    sys  0
    li   v2, 0
    li   v1, 2
    sys  0
bad:
    la   v2, msg_bad
    li   v3, 4
    li   v1, 1
    sys  0
    li   v2, 1
    li   v1, 2
    sys  0
worker:
    mv   v30, v1
    ccall v20, v30
    mv   v3, v1
    li   v2, 1
    li   v1, 8                   ; send the result to task 1; retry if its mailbox is full
retry:
    li   v1, 8
    sys  0
    li   v6, -2
    beq  v1, v6, again
    li   v2, 0
    li   v1, 2
    sys  0
again:
    li   v1, 5
    sys  0
    li   v2, 1
    jmp  retry
msg_ok:  .ascii "gate switching: ok\n"
msg_bad: .ascii "BAD\n"
.align 256
svc:
    clq  v6, [v20 + 128]
    addi v6, v6, 1
    csq  [v20 + 128], v6
    li   v1, 5                   ; yield in the middle of the call
    sys  0
    mv   v1, v6
    cretn
.space 144

gateiso.console:
[kernelloom] Veylith 128-Native v1 booting user program
gate isolation: ok
[kernelloom] user exit 0
gateiso.source:
; Isolated gate call (ccalx / cretx): the callee sees none of the caller's registers and cannot corrupt them.
; The caller fills several registers (including sp) with secrets, calls the service with two arguments (v1, v2), and checks that
;   - the service saw zero in every non-argument register it probed (it reports what it saw),
;   - the service's own clobbering of those registers is invisible after the return,
;   - the arguments arrived and the result came back in v1.
.equ USER_BASE, 0x10000
.org USER_BASE
_start:
    li   sp, 0x1F000
    la   v2, svc
    li   v3, 8
    li   v4, 15                  ; READ | WRITE | NARROW | GATE
    li   v1, 10
    sys  0                       ; capget
    cseal v30, v1
    li   v1, 11
    sys  0                       ; capability mode
    li   v10, 0x1111
    li   v11, 0x2222
    li   v50, 0x5050
    li   v100, 0x100100
    li   v1, 7                   ; argument 1
    li   v2, 5                   ; argument 2
    ccalx v20, v30
    li   v6, 12
    bne  v1, v6, bad             ; 7 + 5, and nothing the service saw was non-zero
    li   v6, 0
    bne  v2, v6, bad             ; v2 carries the service's second result: the count of secrets it saw (must be 0)
    li   v6, 0x1111
    bne  v10, v6, bad
    li   v6, 0x2222
    bne  v11, v6, bad
    li   v6, 0x5050
    bne  v50, v6, bad
    li   v6, 0x100100
    bne  v100, v6, bad
    li   v6, 0x1F000
    bne  sp, v6, bad             ; sp came back untouched even though the service trashed it
    la   v2, msg_ok
    li   v3, 19
    li   v1, 1
    sys  0
    li   v2, 0
    li   v1, 2
    sys  0
bad:
    la   v2, msg_bad
    li   v3, 4
    li   v1, 1
    sys  0
    li   v2, 1
    li   v1, 2
    sys  0
msg_ok:  .ascii "gate isolation: ok\n"
msg_bad: .ascii "BAD\n"
.align 256
svc:                             ; v1, v2 = arguments; v20 = data capability; everything else is zero
    add  v8, v1, v2              ; the real work
    li   v9, 0                   ; count the caller secrets that leaked in
    beq  v10, v0, s1
    addi v9, v9, 1
s1: beq  v11, v0, s2
    addi v9, v9, 1
s2: beq  v50, v0, s3
    addi v9, v9, 1
s3: beq  v100, v0, s4
    addi v9, v9, 1
s4: beq  sp, v0, s5
    addi v9, v9, 1
s5: li   v10, 0xBAD              ; now trash them: none of this may survive the return
    li   v11, 0xBAD
    li   v50, 0xBAD
    li   v100, 0xBAD
    li   sp, 0xBAD
    mv   v1, v8
    mv   v2, v9
    cretx

sigil.console:
[kernelloom] Veylith 128-Native v1 booting user program
Hi
sigil capabilities: ok
[kernelloom] user exit 0
sigil.source:
; Sigil capabilities in Kernelloom: a worker that can reach memory ONLY through a capability it was handed.
; Task 1 mints a 64-byte region (capget), narrows it, and passes the narrowed 128-bit capability to a worker as its spawn
; argument. The worker enters capability mode, writes through the capability, and prints through it with cwrite.
.equ USER_BASE, 0x10000
.org USER_BASE
_start:
    li   sp, 0x1F000
    la   v2, region
    li   v3, 6                   ; 2^6 = 64 bytes, naturally aligned
    li   v4, 7                   ; READ | WRITE | NARROW
    li   v1, 10
    sys  0                       ; capget
    mv   v20, v1                 ; the full-region capability
    li   v21, 1 | 5 << 8 | 32 << 16
    cnarrow v22, v20, v21        ; READ-only window on the upper half (kept to show derivation; not handed out)
    li   v21, 3 | 5 << 8
    cnarrow v23, v20, v21        ; READ|WRITE, lower 32 bytes; narrowed capabilities lose NARROW, so they cannot be widened
    la   v2, worker
    li   v3, 0x1E000
    mv   v4, v23                 ; the capability itself is the argument: all 128 bits travel in one register
    li   v1, 6
    sys  0
    mv   v24, v1
    li   v1, 9                   ; recv: the worker reports when it is done
    sys  0
    mv   v2, v24
    li   v1, 7
    sys  0                       ; join
    la   v5, region
    lq   v6, [v5 + 16]           ; plain load by task 1: the worker's 128-bit write is there
    li   v7, 0x5349474C5F4F4B21F00DFACE0000BEEF
    bne  v6, v7, bad
    la   v2, msg_ok
    li   v3, 23
    li   v1, 1
    sys  0
    li   v2, 0
    li   v1, 2
    sys  0
bad:
    la   v2, msg_bad
    li   v3, 4
    li   v1, 1
    sys  0
    li   v2, 1
    li   v1, 2
    sys  0

worker:                          ; v1 = capability to region[0..32), READ|WRITE
    mv   v20, v1
    li   v1, 11
    sys  0                       ; cmode: from here on raw loads and stores trap
    li   v6, 0x5349474C5F4F4B21F00DFACE0000BEEF
    csq  [v20 + 16], v6          ; 128-bit store through the capability
    li   v8, 0x48                ; "Hi\n" at +0
    csb  [v20 + 0], v8
    li   v8, 0x69
    csb  [v20 + 1], v8
    li   v8, 0x0A
    csb  [v20 + 2], v8
    mv   v2, v20                 ; cwrite: the console buffer is named by the capability, not by a raw pointer
    li   v3, 3
    li   v1, 12
    sys  0
    li   v1, 8                   ; send "done" to task 1
    li   v2, 1
    li   v3, 1
    sys  0
    li   v1, 2
    li   v2, 0
    sys  0
.align 64
region: .space 64
msg_ok:  .ascii "sigil capabilities: ok\n"
msg_bad: .ascii "BAD\n"

sigilforge.console:
[kernelloom] Veylith 128-Native v1 booting user program
[kernelloom] user fault cause=8 tval=168811955464684315858783496655603761322
sigilforge.source:
; Sigil negative test 1: a task in capability mode tries to use a forged capability (a made-up 128-bit value).
; The hardware raises a CAPABILITY trap and Kernelloom reports it as a user fault.
.equ USER_BASE, 0x10000
.org USER_BASE
_start:
    li   sp, 0x1F000
    li   v1, 11
    sys  0
    li   v3, 0x7F0000000000000000000000000000AA       ; a plausible-looking but forged capability
    clq  v4, [v3 + 0]
    li   v2, 0
    li   v1, 2
    sys  0

sigilraw.console:
[kernelloom] Veylith 128-Native v1 booting user program
[kernelloom] user fault cause=8 tval=65664
sigilraw.source:
; Sigil negative test 2: a task in capability mode attempts a raw load. Raw memory access is forbidden there.
.equ USER_BASE, 0x10000
.org USER_BASE
_start:
    li   sp, 0x1F000
    li   v1, 11
    sys  0
    la   v5, data
    lq   v4, [v5 + 0]
    li   v2, 0
    li   v1, 2
    sys  0
.align 16
data: .space 16
